exec_summary: The deepest change in this program is not the software — it is that planning and replenishment stop being individual craft and become shared disciplines. Two teams feel this hardest: buyers, who take on a formal open-to-buy process they have never run, and store leads, who move from calculating orders to trusting and triaging system suggestions.

themes.title: Replenishment moves from spreadsheets to exception management
themes.whats_changing: Store leads stop calculating reorder points by hand each week. The system generates the suggestions from demand signals; leads manage the exceptions — the local events, the odd cases the system can't see.
themes.so_what_script: Here's the honest part. Our store leads are proud of their reorder math, and they don't yet trust a system to know their store. If we don't coach them through the first two cycles, they'll quietly keep the spreadsheets and the benefit never lands. The ask is simple: give us their time for those first two cycles.
asks: Protect store-lead time for coaching during the first two replenishment cycles

themes.title: Buying gets a financial discipline it has never had
themes.whats_changing: Buyers move from planning by instinct in Excel to operating a formal open-to-buy process. This is a net-new capability — there is no current process to improve; the muscle has to be built from scratch.
themes.so_what_script: This one is the steepest learning curve in the program. Nobody here has run open-to-buy before, so this is concept training, not tool training. If we start building that capability at testing, we're too late. We need to start before design closes.
impact_titles: Open-to-buy financial planning introduced as net-new capability
asks: Approve early concept training for buyers, ahead of the testing phase
Name an executive sponsor for the planning-discipline story
Confirm the training calendar can start before buying season
